answer: Sybil resistance can work like a harbor: a ship earns docking rights only with a cargo log stamped at ports it has actually visited, not by painting a new name on its hull. Crossing a dune leaves a trail that independent trackers can follow and confirm, and raven messengers carry attestations between harbors so a claim is checked far from where it was made. A sybil fleet may look large from shore, but ships with no voyages, no stamps, and no trails are turned away at the harbor mouth.
